- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model tends to overpredict; adjust downward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias in early forecast horizon (1–3 days) — if true outcome deviates from 10-day moving average, adjust forecast toward that average.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates upward momentum in bullish sentiment cycles; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if sentiment >0.70 over last 5 days.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive within 3 days, model lags; forecast should shift upward by 1–2% of recent 7-day average within 2–3 days of sentiment change.
